context: Public post on a professional network, written the week after the trip
witness: Visitor from Côte d'Ivoire, short stay, length not given

claims.says: Paid 35,000 FCFA for a ride-hailing trip from Les Almadies to the airport and found the city expensive, advising business travellers to budget generously for transport. No rent or other daily price given; the fare sits at the top of the 20,000 to 30,000 FCFA the site already documents for that run.
Prices can still go up once you are known to be a foreigner; ride-hailing apps were meant to make them clearer.
In Senegal, phone credit from one operator can be bought directly inside a competing mobile-money app, so one app is enough for a top-up.
Sending money from a Côte d'Ivoire wallet to a Senegal wallet of the same mobile-money app cost 1.5 % plus a 0.5 % tax on arrival: 2,000 FCFA on 100,000 FCFA sent, despite the shared currency.

context: Caption and replies by the author of a public video on a social network about where to stay when visiting Cairo
witness: Travel planner who sells trips to Egypt; own time in the city not stated

claims.says: Advises visitors against staying in the pyramids area of Giza: that area has become a tourist trap and gives many people a bad stay, after which they judge Cairo without having set foot in the city itself. Giza as a whole is very large, with many different neighbourhoods, and is not to be judged by that one area.

context: Comment under a public video on a social network about where to stay when visiting Cairo
witness: Visitor who stayed in Giza, away from the tourist area; length and date not given

claims.says: Stayed in Giza away from the tourist area and found it very good. Residents described it as poor compared with the central districts. A good place to see everyday life: neighbourhood markets, street vendors, fruit and vegetables delivered to the door, many friendly residents. Giza is large and should not be judged by the pyramid entrances.
Harassment of visitors exists at the entrances to the pyramids; none reported in the residential part of Giza where the person stayed. The site already mentions scams at tourist places.
Very fresh produce at the Giza markets and good street food everywhere in the area.
